title: Atlas network hardening field guide — VPC, mTLS, SIEM export
content:
Purpose:
This field guide captures a pragmatic, audit-ready set of patterns for Private Deployments (ATLAS) focusing on: VPC topology recommendations, firewall rules (cloud + on-prem snips), enforced mutual TLS strategies, RBAC v2 responsibilities for network configuration, audit-event schema for network enforcement, SIEM export/fetch pattern, and an evidence automation checklist for compliance attestations.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: infra engineers, SREs, security engineers, compliance owners working on private Redwood deployments.
- Scope: network perimeter and east-west controls, TLS termination and service identity, logging/export for SOC/SIEM, automated evidence packaging for audits.

High-level design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Default-deny network posture for all deployment tiers.
- mTLS for all service-to-service traffic inside the cluster/VPC where latency and throughput allow.
- Centralized firewall policy artifacts stored in Git with change reviews and RBAC-controlled apply.
- Line-delimited JSON (NDJSON) SIEM exports of normalized network-audit events.
- Evidence artifacts named deterministically and retained per retention policy.

Threat-model highlights informing controls:
- Unauthorized lateral movement from compromised host/service -> mitigate via segmentation + mTLS + short-lived certs.
- Misconfigured firewall rules introduced by privileged users -> mitigate via RBAC v2 + policy-as-code + pre-deploy validation jobs.
- Missing audit trail for network changes -> mitigate via immutable logs + SIEM ingestion + periodic evidence bundles.

Recommended VPC topologies (patterns):
1) Hub-and-spoke (recommended for multi-tenant enterprise customers)
   - Hub: centralized NAT gateways, logging collectors, shared services (bastion, cert-issuer, SIEM forwarders).
   - Spokes: per-customer or per-service group subnets (private + restricted public egress).
   - Advantages: centralizes egress control, easier global firewall rules.

2) Micro-segmented spoke (recommended for high-regulated customers)
   - Each spoke broken into zones: ingress (front-door), app, data, mgmt.
   - Enforce ACLs between zones; only explicitly allowed flows.

3) Single-tenant dedicated VPC (highest isolation)
   - Minimal shared services; VPC peering or Transit for SIEM/logging to central collectors with encrypted channels.

Minimal subnet layout example (for reference):
- 10.10.0.0/24 - ingress (load balancers / API gateway)
- 10.10.1.0/24 - app-01 (service containers, private IPs)
- 10.10.2.0/24 - data (databases, stateful stores)
- 10.10.254.0/24 - management (bastion, jump hosts)

Firewall and security group rule examples (cloud first):
- Principle: explicitly list source CIDRs and service identities. Default action = DENY.

Example: Ingress LB (GCP/AWS ALB)
- Allow tcp/443 from 0.0.0.0/0 -> target-proxy (TLS terminated at LB)
- Allow tcp/8443 from 10.10.1.0/24 -> internal-control-plane (for healthchecks only)

Example: App service security group (allow only from known front door and mgmt)
- Allow tcp/443 from sg-frontend (service tag) - description: app ingress
- Allow tcp/22 from sg-mgmt/jump (only for emergency debug; must be logged)
- Deny all else

Example: Data subnet firewall (very restricted)
- Allow tcp/5432 from 10.10.1.0/24 (app subnet) - Postgres
- Allow tcp/9200 from 10.10.1.0/24 (search cluster)
- Deny 0.0.0.0/0 for all other ports

On-prem iptables nft sample (drop-by-default):
- nft add table inet redwood-filter
- nft add chain inet redwood-filter input { type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop; }
- nft add rule inet redwood-filter input ct state established,related accept
- nft add rule inet redwood-filter input iifname lo accept
- nft add rule inet redwood-filter input tcp dport {22,443} ip saddr 10.10.254.0/24 accept
- nft add rule inet redwood-filter input tcp dport 8443 ip saddr 10.10.0.0/16 accept

mTLS enforcement patterns (practical guidance):
- Edge termination: terminate TLS at the ingress LB when third-party origination requires public certs; re-encrypt to backend using mTLS.
- Service mesh (recommended): lightweight mesh (e.g., envoy-based) providing automatic mTLS, cert rotation via internal CA.
- Pod-level mTLS: for air-gapped installs use short-lived certs (15-60 min TTL) and an internal CA + auto-rotate agent.
- Certificate validation: validate subject O=redwood-inference, CN=service/<namespace>/<service>, include SAN with IPs and DNS. Log and export client_cert_fingerprint in audit events.

Certificate rotation and issuance policy (baseline):
- Root CA: offline, rotated on major infra events only, document in evidence bundle.
- Intermediate CA: signed by Root; rotate quarterly or on key compromise.
- Leaf certs: TTL 15-60 minutes for service-to-service; automated quick-reissue mechanism.

RBAC v2: who can change network policy (recommended role set):
- network-admin (can propose changes via Git + PR; cannot apply in prod directly)
- infra-release (CI job identity that applies network changes after CI checks pass)
- security-audit (read-only access to firewall rules + logs)
- emergency-operator (can apply in prod but every change must be recorded and auto-reverted by policy if not approved within 4 hours)

Enforcement workflow (policy-as-code):
1) author edits firewall/policy YAML in repo; submits PR to network-config repo.
2) CI runs static validation + simulate (test harness) + linter + RBAC gate (PR approver list).
3) After approvals, infra-release service account runs change-apply job which records apply action into audit log with request_id and approver list.

Network audit event schema (normalized NDJSON per line) - recommended fields (flat list):
- timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
- event_id (UUID v4)
- request_id (correlates change or flow to higher-level request)
- source_ip
- source_identity (service-account or human user email)
- dest_ip
- dest_port
- protocol (TCP/UDP/ICMP)
- action (ALLOW|DENY|REJECT|APPLY|ROLLBACK)
- rule_id (policy id or firewall rule id)
- policy_version
- decision (permit|deny)
- mtls_subject (if present)
- client_cert_fingerprint
- tls_version
- cipher_suite
- bytes_sent
- bytes_received
- latency_ms
- outcome (success|failure)
- error_code (if any)
- component (e.g., gcp-fw, aws-sg, envoy-proxy, nftables)
- actor (identity that initiated change: user or service account)
- trace_id (application-level correlation)

Note: the above is intentionally flat to match SIEM parsers. Field names are lowercase snake_case.

Sample NDJSON line (network audit/change event) - single-line JSON string below:
{"timestamp":"2025-02-01T18:12:09Z","event_id":"2c7f8c9a-78f4-4a1b-b6c1-3a5e2a12c9b7","request_id":"JIRA-PLAT-945-apply","source_ip":"203.0.113.45","source_identity":"infra-release@redwood.com","dest_ip":"10.10.1.12","dest_port":443,"protocol":"TCP","action":"APPLY","rule_id":"fw-2025-1003","policy_version":"v3","decision":"permit","mtls_subject":"CN=service/backend-processor,O=redwood-inference","client_cert_fingerprint":"SHA256:ab12cd...","tls_version":"1.3","cipher_suite":"TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256","bytes_sent":0,"bytes_received":0,"latency_ms":12,"outcome":"success","component":"infra-controlplane","actor":"jonas.meyer@redwood.com","trace_id":"trace-9b1a"}

SIEM export and ingestion guidance:
- Export format: NDJSON gzip rotated daily. File naming: siem-export/yyyy/MM/dd/siem-net-audit-YYYYMMDD-part-<n>.ndjson.gz
- Delivery: push to S3/GCS bucket with server-side encryption, object immutability for retention period, and separate storage class for long-term retention.
- Ingest: SOC pipeline pulls objects and loads into SIEM. Use schema validation and reject files with schema errors. Keep a copy of original objects for forensic purposes.
- Real-time connector: forward critical DENY events and firewall rule applies to SOC via webhook stream (low-latency path) while bulk telemetry goes through batch exports.

Evidence automation: what we collect and why (examples):
- fw-change-log-YYYYMMDD.ndjson - every firewall apply operation including PR id, approver list, and CI job id (required for change audit).
- vpc-flow-YYYYMMDD.part.ndjson.gz - VPC flow logs for spoke; used for lateral movement detection and throughput baselines.
- mtls-cert-inventory-YYYYMMDD.csv - certificate serials, subject, issuer, not_before, not_after, fingerprint (for attestation).
- policy-repo-commit-<sha>.tar.gz - snapshot of policy-as-code repo (signed).
- apply-automation-runbook-<timestamp>.md - log of automation job runs + stdout/stderr captured.

Evidence naming / retention conventions:
- namespace: evidence/<tenant-or-deploy>/component/YYYYMMDD/<artifact-type>-<timestamp>.ext
- example: evidence/atlas-prod/vpc/2025-02-02/vpc-flow-20250202.part1.ndjson.gz
- retention: align with customer/regulator; default retention 1 year, ability to enable 7/14 years for regulated customers.

Automated packaging job (reference design):
- Trigger: daily cron in infra-release account + on-demand via runbook.
- Steps: 1) snapshot current policy repo (git archive) 2) collect SIEM-ready NDJSON slices for last 24h 3) gather cert-inventory from cert-issuer API 4) take quick topology dump (subnets, routes, firewall rules) 5) compute and sign manifest (hashes + signer identity) 6) upload package to evidences-bucket/encrypted and notify compliance slack channel + create JIRA evidence artifact.

Pre-deploy checklist (must-pass before production apply):
- [ ] PR in network-config repo reviewed by two approvers (at least one security engineer).
- [ ] CI validation passed (static lint + simulate + negative tests).
- [ ] Apply job approved by infra-release service account and recorded.
- [ ] Impact analysis completed (list of affected subnets/services)
- [ ] Nightly canary window defined for higher-risk rules

Periodic audit checklist (monthly/quarterly):
- [ ] Validate RBAC roles and membership (remove stale access).
- [ ] Verify SIEM ingestion health and schema conformance for last 90 days.
- [ ] Verify certificate rotation cadence and no certs older than policy window.
- [ ] Review evidence export packaging — spot check manifests and hashes.
- [ ] Run automated penetration checks against allowed rules (no unintended open ports).

Incident response quick commands (for operators):
- Quarantine a host: add ephemeral deny rule at edge gateway: "deny from <host-ip>/32 to 10.10.0.0/16" and open ticket JIRA-SEC-INC-xxxx.
- Revoke service cert: call cert-issuer revoke API with serial; trigger rolling restart to force re-issue.
- Export last 2 hours of VPC flows for host: run flow-exporter --ip <host-ip> --since now-2h --format ndjson | gzip > tmp/host-flow-$(date -I).ndjson.gz

Small operational ASCII diagram (logical):
            [Internet]
               |
           +---+---+
           |  LB   |  (public 443)
           +---+---+
               | (re-encrypt mTLS)
        -----------------------
        |        Hub VPC       |  (10.0.0.0/16)
        |  +----------------+  |
        |  | SIEM / Logs    |  |
        |  +----------------+  |
        |     |      |         |
        -----------------------
         |      |      |
     SpokeA  SpokeB  SpokeC   (10.10.x.0/24 per spoke)
     app     apps    dbs

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Avoid long-lived root or intermediate certs for workload identity — short TTLs prevent stealth lateral persistence.
- Do not rely solely on IP-based allow lists for services with dynamic addresses; prefer service identity (mTLS subject) + policy.
- Ensure SIEM schema forwards client_cert_fingerprint and mtls_subject — useful for post-incident mapping to service identity.
- When enabling emergency-operator apply, attach automatic revert job: if manual apply not approved in N hours, revert.

Appendix A — quick mapping to compliance artifacts for auditors:
- Where is the evidence of change control? -> evidence/<deploy>/policy-repo-commit-<sha>.tar.gz + fw-change-log-YYYYMMDD.ndjson
- Where are network logs? -> siem-export/yyyy/MM/dd/siem-net-audit-YYYYMMDD-part-*.ndjson.gz
- Certificate attestation? -> mtls-cert-inventory-YYYYMMDD.csv + signed manifest
- RBAC and approver list? -> iam-export-roles-YYYYMMDD.csv + PR review history (link in manifest)

Appendix B — short sample automation CLI snippets (pseudo):
- Generate exported evidence package:
  infra-release@runner:~/scripts$ ./package_evidence.sh --deploy atlas-prod --since 2025-02-01 --out /tmp/atlas-evidence-20250201.tar.gz

- Validate NDJSON schema locally:
  $ jq empty < sample_event.ndjson || echo "schema error"

Feedback and next steps:
- This doc is a field guide to be adopted/adapted by each customer deployment. We should add a small reference implementation (terraform + cert-issuer) in the infra repo and a test harness for NDJSON validation.
- Action: attach PR template for network-config changes and add a required security approver group.

Last updated by: Asha Ramanathan (asha.r@redwood.com) on 2025-02-03
